facts.fact_text: On 15 April 2007 in St Petersburg a coalition of opposition groups organised an anti-government rally to campaign before the forthcoming parliamentary elections.
The applicants attended the rally on 15 April 2007 at Pionerskaya Square in St Petersburg.
The site of the rally at Pionerskaya Square was cordoned off by several rows of police officers.
According to the applicants, the applicants saw the riot police (Special Purpose Squad, ОМОН) running towards them and indiscriminately hitting all those around them.
According to the applicants, the police pushed civilians into a small park.
During the events of 15 April 2007, the first applicant was severely beaten by a riot police officer.
During the events of 15 April 2007, the third applicant was hit by a riot police officer with a rubber truncheon to the face.
According to the Government, at the end of the rally a group of approximately 60 persons under the flags of the National Bolshevik Party attempted to break through the police cordon.

According to the Government, the group of approximately 60 persons under the flags of the National Bolshevik Party attempted to lead an unauthorised march via Zagorodnyy Prospect towards Moskovskiy Prospect.
According to the Government, persons in the group of approximately 60 persons under the flags of the National Bolshevik Party threw bottles and other objects at the police officers.

According to the Government's version of events, the riot police (Special Purpose Squad, ОМОН) had to use force in order to disperse the particular group of protesters who attempted to break through the police cordon and restore public order.
The Government submitted that 6,100 police officers were deployed at the rally on 15 April 2007.
The Government submitted that among the 6,100 police officers deployed, 400 were officers from the Special Purpose Squad (ОМОН), referred to as the riot police.
According to the applicants, the applicants saw the riot police (Special Purpose Squad, ОМОН) running towards them and indiscriminately hitting all those around them.
During the events of 15 April 2007, the first applicant was severely beaten by a riot police officer.
The riot police officer left the first applicant lying unconscious.
At the Mariinskiy Hospital the first applicant was diagnosed with a closed fracture of the seventh rib, traumatic pneumothorax, a closed craniocerebral injury, and brain concussion.
The third applicant was subsequently diagnosed with a craniocerebral injury sustained on 15 April 2007, concussion, closed fractures of the nose bones and the right cheek bone.

The Oktyabrskiy District Court of St Petersburg noted that during the investigation it was established that on 15 April 2007 some unidentified police officers had exceeded their official powers and beaten a number of protesters.

The Oktyabrskiy District Court of St Petersburg noted that the victims and witnesses could not identify the police officers due to the fact that the officers were wearing helmets and had no identification markings.
The Oktyabrskiy District Court of St Petersburg found that none of the investigative measures taken allowed identification of the perpetrators.
In April 2007 the applicants submitted complaints to the St Petersburg prosecution authorities about police brutality.
In May 2007 the applicants submitted additional complaints to the St Petersburg prosecution authorities about police brutality.
On 21 June 2007 a criminal case was opened in relation to the events of 15 April 2007.
On 15 June 2007 a domestic court found that the prosecution authorities had failed to comply with the time-limits established for examination of individual complaints.
On 15 June 2007 a domestic court found that the prosecution authorities had unlawfully denied the applicants access to the case-file of the enquiry.
On 15 June 2007 a domestic court found that the prosecution authorities had failed to ensure the applicants' procedural rights during the criminal investigation.
On 15 November 2007 a domestic court found that the prosecution authorities had failed to comply with the time-limits established for examination of individual complaints.
On 15 November 2007 a domestic court found that the prosecution authorities had unlawfully denied the applicants access to the case-file of the enquiry.
On 15 November 2007 a domestic court found that the prosecution authorities had failed to ensure the applicants' procedural rights during the criminal investigation.
Between December 2007 and June 2009 the criminal investigation was suspended seven times due to failure to identify the police officers who had attacked the applicants.
On 25 June 2009 the criminal proceedings were stayed because the perpetrators could not be identified.

The first applicant challenged the decision of 25 June 2009 to stay the criminal proceedings, arguing that the investigator had not taken all the necessary steps to identify the police officers involved in the attacks.
The Oktyabrskiy District Court of St Petersburg rejected the first applicant's complaint against the decision to stay the criminal proceedings.
